Technology Action ​ / ​ 4.3.1 Technology track row bonus 4.4 Bonus tokens ​ 5 Turn End 6 Game End Overview Zenith is tug-of-war style game in which you and your opponent battle for control of five planets, competing to be the first to achieve one of three victory conditions: 3= Absolute Victory : Gain 3 influence tokens from the same planet. 4≠ Democratic Victory : Gain 4 influence tokens from different planets. 5 Popular Victory : Gain 5 influence tokens from any combination of planets. Influence ​ +1 influence on a planet = move that planet's influence token 1 space towards you. When an influence token reaches your edge of the board, you keep it and a new token is placed on the planet. Excess influence when arriving at the edge of the board is lost. Planet colours ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Mercury Venus Terra Mars Jupiter Setup 1st player is decided randomly. 2nd player gains 1 Terra influence (moving 1🡇 space towards their control zone). Both players start with 4 cards. Turn Structure Select 1 from your hand to use for one of three actions: 1. Diplomacy Action ​ Discard 1 to gain the Leader Badge ​ (silver side), plus the diplomacy bonus for the faction of the card you are discarding. Robot : Take the Leader badge and gain 1 Zenithium. Human : Take the Leader badge and gain 3 Credits. Animod : Take the Leader badge and mobilize 2 cards. If you already have ​ , turn it to the gold side ​ . Each side of the Leader Badge increases your hand size by one 5 6 . If you already have ​ , your hand size remains at 6. 2. Influence Action 🡇 Spend the credits ​ cost of a card to play that card on your stack and carry out the card's effects (left to right). All cards provide 1🡇 for its planet plus other effects shown on the card. Effects range from gaining more influence in the same or other planets, gaining new cards on your stacks, removing cards from your opponent's stacks or even stealing cards from your opponent's stacks onto your stacks. Credit Discount -# For each card previously placed in your stack for that planet, -1 from the card cost. e.g. if your Mercury stack has 5 , an 8 cost would cost 8 − 5 = 3 . If you have more cards than the cost, it is free (but do not gain ​ ). 3. Technology Action ​ / ​ Discard the card to progress your Tech marker ( ​ / ​ ) on the technology track for the faction of the card (Animod, Human or Robot). To carry out this action you have to spend the required Zenithium ( ​ ) to pay for the next level on the respective technology track. When your Tech marker progresses to the next level, gain the effect of that level plus all previous levels on that faction's track. Markers can only move one level per turn. Technology track row bonus When you develop all three technology tracks to the same level , you gain influence on a planet of your choice: Tech level bonus Level 1 Level 2 Level 3 1🡇 2🡇 3🡇 One-time bonus. Not levels 4 and 5. Bonus tokens ​ There are 16 bonus tokens in the game; 8 face up and 8 face down in a draw pile. Each planet has a face up bonus. 1st player to gain ​ for a planet gains it. Each technology track level 2 space has a face up bonus. 1st player to arrive at level 2 on a technology track gains it. Face down bonuses can also be achieved in other ways. Used bonuses are not replaced. community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] Another version of “advance on these various tracks”. I prefer the mild tug-of-war aspect here and the multi-use card play is often clever. Appropriately restrictive in how one must manage (or acquire) their resources. Need many more plays to determine if the cards feel totally balanced or not and also assess whether the game has any real staying power.  [b]Update:[/b] No desire to return to this.

[Rating: 1/10] Eurogamers would probably like this a lot. For me, there was too little interaction, but too many euro symbols and combi-building. A tug of war where I mostly don’t care what the opponent does. And then effects get discounted on the main board (eh) or multiplied on the side board (woah!). At least there’s no VP.  I do like the artwork a lot, it has a nice style with a lot of variety. But you spend most of the game trying to study the effects instead of looking at art…. I guess that’s a problem with every eurogame though.

[Rating: 3/10] Unbalanced and swingy. This is one of those games where luck matters more than strategy. Why? You can have a good starting game and be up 3 to 0 but then be handed the worst cards over and over and over again while your opponent ends up with stronger cards. No draw engine, no way to drop to hand for new cards. Poorly designed and honestly not sure how anyone is rating this above a 5.

[Rating: 3/10] BGA. 5 is average for me. So 6 is above average. Combo of bringing tokens to sides with multi use cards. Interesting and will play if in the mood. UPDATE: more plays has revelaed how frustrating this game can be. Takes too long for what it is doing / offers. Lowering ranking to 3. Has really started to bug me.

[Rating: 3/10] I don't understand the hype. The instructions and iconography are terrible. The graphics don't support the theme at all. You're dependent on your starting hand. The game board is ugly. It takes far too long for what it is. The combinations are at least somewhat nice.

[Rating: 3/10] Once you have played 10 games you know exactly how to win and the game become only a game based on luck when you take you cards... No interest.

[Rating: 4/10] Un jeu de course et de tir à la corde un peu trop tarabiscoté pour moi, trop abstrait, trop chargé en icônes de partout. Même si c’est relativement simple et fluide, les parties m’ont paru bien longues. Une déception après le génial Captain Flip paru l’an dernier chez l’éditeur.

[Rating: 4/10] Zenith has all the pretense of a quick yet shrewd tug-of-war game that rewards careful card play. But it's just a bit too random for my liking. There's a few too many uncontrollable variables to manage with all the different colours, card types. multiple currencies and plethora of tracks. It's really a very simple game, but all these variables (and all the symbols) make it look more complex than it is.  It;s biggest problem is that it suffers from the 'lack of the right card at the right time' problem. You can play yourself into an interesting position and then just be screwed because you can'

[Rating: 4/10] Fiddly and very luck-dependent based on the size of the shared deck and the number of lanes (5). Also way too many icons for a game of this weight.  Would always rather play Air, Land & Sea or Lost Cities over Zenith.

[Rating: 4/10] Testé en aout 2026 : Mécanique où on doit récupérer des planetes grace à des cartes sur des lignes (comme la ligne de boucliers militaires dans 7 wonders).  Pénible car les planettes vont et viennent vers soi ou son adversaire en fonction des coups joués.
